chance_note: cells_expected_by_chance = 5% of cells (raw p<0.05 expected if every cell were null); BH at q=0.10 expects at most 10% of its passes to be false.
intro: 325,896 random entries on 34 instruments, 2017-2022 sessions (built from 2016-10-24), each taken long at the ask and short at the bid; stops touched on the M1 bid/ask path. 2023 onward is not looked at.

Holds across: on the mid, a σ stop is touched at the random-walk rate at 1σ (16.5% vs 16.3% to 22:00). The bid/ask path adds the spread on top (18.3%), +1 to +4 points at every size, every year and every class except indices.

Holds across: the tails are fat. Tight stops (0.25σ) are touched less than a random walk (63% vs 66% on the mid), and wide ones far more (2σ: 2.5% vs 1.4%; 3σ: 0.5% vs 0.05%). The curve is smooth, with no size where behaviour changes, which matches the stage 2 result of no noise threshold.

Local to class: FX crosses carry the largest excess (+3 points at 1σ, mostly spread in σ terms). Indices sit at or below the random walk (DE30 -2.1, NQ -1.1), so their paths are smoother than their σ suggests.

Time left holds across every hour: the same 1σ stop placed at 00:00 is touched 32% of the time by 22:00, at 12:00 17%, at 16:00 5%. Real tracks the vol clock about 2 points above it. Counting hours left would understate it by up to 6 points around midday. (The 29.5% quoted elsewhere was session high/low from the open; from the open on bid/ask it is 32.2%.)

Fixed width vs σ: a fixed-width stop swings with the regime (+12.9 points over the walk when turbulent, -3.4 in the low-σ tercile; year SD 4.6 points). The σ stop stays within about 2.5 points of the walk (year SD 0.7). This is the one clear case for vol-scaling a stop.

Error-scaled stop (σ × exp(recent forecast error)): too noisy to tell overall. Year SD is 0.45 vs 0.73 points, but the difference range crosses 0. It is a little better in calm regimes and reverses in turbulent ones (Brier worse, BH-passing). The half-life/strength sweep shows a peak at short look-backs and weak scaling, not a plateau.

+1 lag: delaying σ by a session changes nothing (2.18 vs 2.03 points over the walk; same year SD). The σ-vs-fixed effect is about the slow vol level, not same-day alignment. It survives, but it does not show day-specific information.

Overshoot: weekday stops gap on 3% of hits, with a median of 0.006σ but a heavy tail (GPD ξ ≈ 0.34, p99 0.69σ). Weekend opens gap on 81% of hits, with p99 3.9σ, ξ ≈ 0.06 and a mean net loss of 1.38R vs 1.00R. Gap risk is a weekend size question, not a stop-distance question.

For placement: put the stop in σ units, read its touch odds from the vol clock for the time left, add the spread in σ (largest in crosses and quiet regimes), and size weekend holds for a ~1.4R average stopped loss. Nothing here says any stop distance has an edge.

charts.title: How often a stop is touched by 22:00, by stop size
charts.note: All 34 instruments, random entries long and short. Compare real mid with the random walk: below it for small stops (0.25-0.5σ), on it at 1σ, above it for wide stops (fat tails: 3σ is touched ~10x more often than a random walk says). The bid/ask line sits 1-4 points above the mid line at every size: that is the spread. The curves are smooth, with no step at any size. The error-scaled stop sits on the plain one.

charts.title: 1σ stop by holding horizon: real vs random walk vs fixed width
charts.note: All instruments. A 1σ stop is rarely touched inside a few hours; over 5 sessions most are. Compare the first bar with the random walk in each group: the shortfall is in points, and grows with the horizon until saturation. The fixed-width stop is a trailing 252-session median σ, the same price distance every day.

charts.title: Each instrument: 1σ stop touch rate minus random walk, held to 22:00
charts.note: Below 0 = touched less than a random walk with the instrument's own intraday variance profile. 95% date-block range. Look for any instrument above 0 (a stop there is hit more than geometry says).

charts.title: Class pooled: touch rate minus random walk at 0.5σ, 1σ, 2σ
charts.note: 0 = random walk. Same sign in every class and horizon = holds across. The size of the shortfall peaks at mid stops (where the random-walk rate is near 50%) and fades at the extremes.

charts.title: London time of entry: 1σ stop touch rate minus random walk
charts.note: Entry time in Europe/London. The random walk already uses the intraday profile, so a quiet Asia hour is not penalised; what is left is how bursty each window is beyond its average variance.

charts.title: Time left: the same 1σ stop placed later in the session, held to 22:00
charts.note: The same 1σ stop placed at 01:00 vs 18:00. Benchmarks: the random walk on the vol clock (variance left in the day), on a linear clock (hours left), and the naive full-day 2Φ(−1)=31.7%. The real line follows the vol clock, about 2 points above it (the spread); the linear clock is up to 6 points too low around midday.

charts.title: Vol regime: 1σ stop touch rate minus random walk, held to 22:00
charts.note: C.OG Lesson 05 regime, past only (vol63 > 1.25× its 252-session median for 21+ sessions). Effective sample = episodes (per-instrument runs; mean length 222 sessions, used as the bootstrap block). σ terciles: σ vs its own 252-session median. Look at the fixed-width bar: it swings with the regime; the σ stops stay near each other.

charts.title: Year by year: 1σ stop touch rate minus random walk, held to 22:00
charts.note: All instruments. 0 = the random-walk rate. A steady stop keeps the same bar height every year; the fixed-width stop is the benchmark for what an unscaled stop does.

charts.title: Stability: spread of the 1σ touch rate across years (SD, points), held to 22:00
charts.note: Lower = the stop's touch rate is more predictable year to year. Rows 1-4 are the SD for each stop; rows 5-7 are the difference vs the plain σ stop with a 95% date-block range (below 0 = steadier than plain σ). The delayed-σ row is the +1 lag check.

charts.title: Plateau check: error-scaled stop vs plain σ stop, by look-back and strength
charts.note: 1σ stop, held to 22:00, all instruments. 0 = no better than the plain σ stop at matching the random-walk touch rate; below 0 = closer. A flat line near the same value across half-lives = plateau; a dip at one setting = peak.

charts.title: +1 lag check: 1σ touch rate minus random walk with inputs delayed one more session
charts.note: If today's σ carries real information about today's path, delaying it should move the touch rate away from the random walk and widen the spread. If the delayed bar matches the undelayed one, the result is an alignment artefact.

charts.title: Overshoot past the stop when the bar opened beyond it (bid/ask), in daily σ
charts.note: Stops hit within 5 sessions. A fill at the stop has overshoot 0; only stops where the bar opened beyond the stop are shown. Benchmark: Kou-Wang memoryless overshoot = the same size at every stop distance. Weekday gaps are tiny; weekends are the tail.

charts.title: Gap overshoot past a 1σ stop (log10 of daily σ)
charts.note: Stops that gapped. GPD on the top 10%: weekday ξ = 0.339, weekend ξ = 0.058 (ξ > 0 = heavy tail, ξ = 0 = exponential as Kou-Wang assume). The right hump is weekend opens.

charts.title: Loss when stopped, in R: gross (mid) vs net (one spread)
charts.note: Stops hit within 24 hours. 1.00 = filled exactly at the stop. Gross above 1 is the overshoot; net minus gross is one spread in R, which grows as the stop tightens.

charts.title: 12 random entries whose 0.5σ stop was touched on the bid/ask path
charts.note: Picked by seed among random entries whose stop (0.5σ = 1R) was touched by 22:00, not by result. Path is the mid in R; the stop is triggered on the bid (long) or ask (short), so it can trigger before the mid line reaches -1. Benchmark: on a random walk, after the touch the rest of the path is a coin flip.
